## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)

The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:

- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
- Kumiko Nishioka, *Mahler Functions and Transcendence* (1996), Theorem 5.1.7,
  is the standard reference for the rational--transcendental dichotomy for
  `k`-Mahler functions defined by a linear functional equation. Bell, Coons and
  Rowland, arXiv:1210.2070v2, Corollary 8, gives an open-access restatement and
  a new proof.
- The equation `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is quadratic in `F` and therefore
  outside that linear class. Keiji Nishioka's 1985 nonlinear class
  `f(z^p) = R(z,f(z))` is the applicable result, with `p = 2` and
  `R(z,Y) = Y^2/H(z)`. This algebraic-to-rational step is prior work and is not
  a contribution of the paper.
- Springer keeps the cited 1985 pages 330--335 behind subscription, and
  Unpaywall reported no open-access copy; this audit does not record a
  first-hand check of the printed text.
- The paper's claimed Mahler contribution is limited to the input-only divisor
  estimate for the multiplicative certificate, its sharp lower-bound family
  and realizable transfer, and the supporting explicit height and fixed-base
  integer bit analysis. Bare existence and decidability are prior, and the
  Pade step is largely standard rational reconstruction after a degree cap is
  known. The tier-carrying claim is the cross-base odd-Adams-invariant
  abelian-two-group dynamical inverse theorem.

In particular, the paper does not claim originality for the general
algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,
for Frobenius-class products or equidistribution, or for the general
periodic-data dictionary. This boundary matches the introduction and
conclusion of the present manuscript.

## General-p multiplicative Mahler priority correction (15 August 2026)

A new search was made before extending the effective theorem from `p=2` to
arbitrary fixed `p >= 2`.  It covered the arXiv API, Crossref, the full texts
of arXiv:1612.05518 and arXiv:2403.11545, the author-hosted full text of the
ISSAC 2022 paper below, zbMATH/Open search results, and exact-title web
searches for combinations of `rational solutions`, `Mahler equation`,
`multiplicative`, `summability`, `Riccati`, and `first-order factors`.
OpenAlex returned a depleted daily API budget and ACM's landing page returned
a browser challenge, so neither was treated as negative evidence.  Crossref
metadata and the author-hosted paper supplied the primary record instead.

The decisive antecedents are:

- F. Chyzak, T. Dreyfus, P. Dumas, and M. Mezzarobba, *Computing
  solutions of linear Mahler equations*, Math. Comp. 87 (2018), 2977--3021,
  DOI `10.1090/mcom/3359`, arXiv:`1612.05518`.  Its abstract and Section 3
  give algorithms for rational solutions of linear Mahler equations.
- C. E. Arreche and Y. Zhang, *Mahler Discrete Residues and Summability for
  Rational Functions*, ISSAC 2022, 525--533, DOI
  `10.1145/3476446.3536186`.  Its abstract and Main Theorem give a complete
  effective obstruction to deciding whether a given rational `f(z)` equals
  `g(z^p)-g(z)` for rational `g`.  Its introduction explicitly notes that
  the 2018 linear-Mahler rational-solution algorithm also decides this
  certificate problem.
- F. Chyzak, T. Dreyfus, P. Dumas, and M. Mezzarobba, *First-order factors
  of linear Mahler operators*, J. Symbolic Comput. 130 (2025), 102424, DOI
  `10.1016/j.jsc.2025.102424`, arXiv:`2403.11545`.  Its Riccati monomials are
  products of successive shifts.  It is adjacent, but it is not needed for
  the reduction below.
- C. Pegis, *Rational Solutions of a Nonlinear Functional Equation Related
  to Mahler's Equation*, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 199 (1996), 489--494, DOI
  `10.1006/jmaa.1996.0156`, treats the different equation
  `F(z^2)=A F(z)+B+C/F(z)` with constant coefficients.

The multiplicative decision problem is not formally separate from the first
two algorithms.  Put `H=P0/P1`, let `sigma f(z)=f(z^p)`, and define
`u=z R'/R`.  Direct logarithmic differentiation proves

```
(sigma-1)u = (z/p) H'/H.                                      (1)
```

Thus Arreche--Zhang directly decides and constructs the possible `u`.  The
2018 homogeneous algorithm also applies: for nonzero right-hand side `f`, any
solution of `(sigma-1)u=f` satisfies
`(sigma-(sigma f)/f)(sigma-1)u=0`, after which one filters the rational
solution space by the original affine equation.

The converse is also effective, so this is a reduction rather than a
one-way necessary condition. Additive solutions are determined only up to a
constant. After replacing `u` by its unique representative with `u(0)=0`, it
comes from a normalized `R in Q(z)` exactly when `u/z` is regular at zero,
has no polynomial part, and has only simple finite poles with integer
residues. Necessity
is the standard partial-fraction form of a rational logarithmic derivative.
For sufficiency, Galois invariance groups poles with the same integer residue
into rational irreducible factors; their normalized product gives
`R'/R=u/z` and `R(0)=1`.  Equation (1) then says that
`R(z^p)/(H(z)R(z)^p)` has zero logarithmic derivative.  Its value at zero is
one, so it is identically one.

Consequently, bare decidability of the multiplicative rational-solution
problem is already subsumed after this non-obvious transformation.  The
nontrivial surviving core is the input-only degree bound of sharp order
`D log D` for the multiplicative certificate itself, together with its lower-
bound family and dynamically realizable transfer. The explicit height and
fixed-`p` integer bit bounds are useful quantitative additions. The affine
Pade calculation is a direct implementation of standard rational
reconstruction once the degree cap is known, and exact rejection is necessary
for correctness rather than a separate novelty claim.

## Frobenius-class product and Axiom A flow audit (8 August 2026)

This additional audit was performed before attempting any flow extension.
The arXiv Atom API, Crossref, Google Scholar, zbMATH Open, and the reference
lists of the principal antecedents were searched for combinations of
`Frobenius class`, `Mertens`, `closed orbits`, `finite group extension`,
`Galois covering`, and `Axiom A flow`.  The exact arXiv queries for
`"Axiom A flows" AND Chebotarev` and for `"Frobenius class" AND
"closed orbits"` returned zero records; the broader query `"closed orbits"
AND Mertens` returned the later sofic-shift note arXiv:2202.03075.  Crossref
confirmed the records and citation trails for Sharp (1991), DOI
`10.1007/BF01237365`, and Parry--Pollicott (1986), DOI
`10.1017/S0143385700003333`.  Google Scholar returned those two works and
Mohamed--Noorani (1999) as the relevant exact-title results; subsequent
requests encountered Scholar's automated-traffic challenge.  zbMATH Open
record `0761.58041` supplies a review and full reference list for Sharp's
Mertens product theorem, and record `0626.58006` states the Frobenius-class
Chebotarev theorem for finite Galois coverings of Axiom A flows.

The official Mohamed--Noorani PDF was checked directly, including Theorem 1
on pp. 124--125 and all seven references.  Theorem 1 already proves a
Frobenius-class Mertens product for closed orbits of a subshift of finite type,
with exponent `|C|/|G|` and an explicit constant written in Artin-L terms.
The present manuscript cites it in the abstract, introduction, theorem-local
comparison, formal correction theorem, conclusion, and bibliography.  It
states plainly that product existence and the exponent are prior art, isolates
the invalid replacement of `chi(g_gamma)` by `chi(g_gamma^r)`, and separately
repairs the missing extension-level mixing/strict-gap hypothesis.  No citation
change was needed.

The proposed leading-product analogue for Axiom A flows is not a defensible
tier-up target.  Sharp already proves the unrestricted Axiom A Mertens product,
while Parry--Pollicott prove Frobenius-class density for mixing finite Galois
extensions; the class-restricted leading product is a direct synthesis of that
analytic framework.  There is also a formulation problem: a continuous (hence
Holder) cocycle `c:X x R -> G` into a discrete finite group is trivial, since
`t -> c(x,t)` is continuous and equals the identity at zero.  The non-trivial
flow category is a finite principal covering with monodromy, or equivalently a
finite cocycle on a Poincare return map/Markov coding.  In that correct
category, the genuinely defensible increment of this manuscript remains the
fixed-primitive-label correction to the constant and its exact finite-state
consequences, not a new Mertens theorem or a new Axiom A leading asymptotic.
As with the earlier audit, this is evidence delimiting the novelty claim, not
a proof of absolute priority.

## Scope and method

The search concerned the following precise question: for a fixed finite directed
graph and a finite-group one-step edge cocycle, does the family of irreducible
twisted characteristic polynomials determine the cocycle up to continuous
Livsic cohomology, and is there a published necessary-and-sufficient invariant
for that property?  This is narrower than conjugacy or flow equivalence of
`G`-SFTs and narrower than recovery of unmarked periodic data.

The arXiv Atom API (`https://export.arxiv.org/api/query`) was queried directly.
The following exact searches each returned `opensearch:totalResults = 0`:

- `all:"twisted determinant" AND all:"shift of finite type"`;
- `all:"Livsic" AND all:"finite group" AND all:"subshift"`;
- `all:"inverse rigidity" AND all:"dynamical zeta"`;
- `all:"periodic data" AND all:"non-abelian cocycle"`;
- `all:"G-SFT" AND all:"zeta"`.

The API feed timestamp was `2026-08-01T16:29:26--27Z`.  Subsequent broader
API requests were rate-limited with HTTP 429; this limitation is material and
precludes treating the search as proof of absolute priority.  Exact-title and
DOI searches were therefore cross-checked against Crossref and OpenAlex, and
the manuscript's existing adjacent bibliography was reviewed entry by entry.

## Closest prior work

1. M. Boyle and S. Schmieding, *Finite group extensions of shifts of finite
   type: K-theory, Parry and Livsic*, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 37 (2017),
   1026--1059, DOI `10.1017/etds.2015.87`, arXiv:`1503.02050`.

   This is the closest comparison.  It studies periodic-data invariants and
   topological conjugacy classes of finite-group extensions, proves that zeta
   data can be compatible with infinitely many non-conjugate extensions, and
   gives computable complete invariants for periodic data.  It does not state
   the fixed-named-edge Livsic fiber cardinality used here, the one-step
   transfer-memory reduction, or the formula
   `m! / product_g n_g!` for finite-abelian bouquet cocycles.  The present
   paper cites this result as an antecedent and does not present its
   K-theoretic or `G`-SFT conjugacy results as new.

2. J. Epperlein, *Eventual conjugacy of free inert G-SFTs*, Ergodic Theory
   Dynam. Systems (First View, 2026), DOI `10.1017/etds.2026.10309`,
   arXiv:`2309.08512`.

   This concerns eventual conjugacy of a named subclass of `G`-SFTs, not
   determinant fibers on a fixed edge presentation.

3. R. Dougall and R. Sharp, *Anosov flows, growth rates on covers and group
   extensions of subshifts*, Invent. Math. 223 (2021), 445--483,
   DOI `10.1007/s00222-020-00994-3`, arXiv:`1904.01423`.

   This supplies adjacent group-extension and spectral-growth context, not an
   inverse classification of edge cocycles.

4. V. Berthe, H. Goulet-Ouellet, C.-F. Nyberg-Brodda, D. Perrin, and
   K. Petersen, *Density of group languages in shift spaces*, Ergodic Theory
   Dynam. Systems (First View, 2026), DOI `10.1017/etds.2026.10318`,
   arXiv:`2403.17892`.

   This is adjacent finite-group symbolic dynamics but does not address
   twisted-determinant inverse rigidity.

conjugate weights, and cohomology; that distinction is respected in the new
proof.  The Numdam bibliographic record was used for the Parry--Pollicott
Asterisque volume because no DOI was located.

## Novelty assessment

No searched source states the following combined result: continuous
cohomology between finite-group one-step edge cocycles on an essential edge
shift reduces to vertex gauge; the exact twisted-determinant rigidity
obstruction is the cardinality of a full-Wedderburn spectral fiber in
`Hom(pi_1(|Gamma|),G)/G`; and on a finite-abelian `m`-loop bouquet that
cardinality equals `m! / product_g n_g!`, with every primitive non-trivial
abelian bouquet extension consequently non-rigid.

The defensible novelty claim is therefore limited to this fixed-presentation
spectral-cohomology classification and its closed abelian-bouquet evaluation.
The general multiplicity-one criterion is an intrinsic finite reformulation,
not a claim that periodic-data or `G`-SFT classification was previously
unknown.  Absolute priority cannot be certified by a finite database search;
the zero-result API queries and the targeted comparison above provide
evidence of novelty, not a logical proof of it.

## Effective rational Mahler coboundary audit

An additional search was performed on 8 August 2026 for the normalized
nonlinear equation
`P0(z) R(z)^2 = P1(z) R(z^2)`. The arXiv Atom API returned zero results for
each of

- `all:"rational solutions" AND all:"Mahler equation"`;
- `all:"Mahler coboundary"`;
- `all:"multiplicative coboundary" AND all:Mahler`;
- `all:"rational function" AND all:"f(z^k)"`.

The broader query `all:"Mahler equations" AND all:algorithm AND
all:rational` returned four records. The only directly adjacent one was
F. Chyzak, T. Dreyfus, P. Dumas, and M. Mezzarobba, *Computing solutions of
linear Mahler equations*, Math. Comp. 87 (2018), 2977--3021,
DOI `10.1090/mcom/3359`, arXiv:`1612.05518`. It treats linear Mahler
operators, not the nonlinear normalized equation above. The same authors'
*First-order factors of linear Mahler operators*, arXiv:`2403.11545`, computes
infinite-product solutions and factors of linear Mahler operators; its
Hermite--Pade step likewise does not state the divisor bound, coefficient
height bound, or nonlinear Pade criterion used here.

Crossref and zbMATH Open were queried with the phrases `rational solutions
Mahler equations`, `effective rationality Mahler functions algorithm`,
`rational solutions nonlinear Mahler equation`, and `algebraic Mahler equation
rational solution algorithm`. The potentially closest title was C. Pegis,
*Rational solutions of a nonlinear functional equation related to Mahler's
equation*, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 199 (1996), 489--494,
DOI `10.1006/jmaa.1996.0156`. The zbMATH review identifies its equation as
`F(z^2)=A F(z)+B+C/F(z)` for constants `A,B,C`; it is not the equation
`F(z^2)=(P0/P1)F(z)^2` and supplies none of the present input-dependent
bounds. No searched record states the effective normalized rational
coboundary theorem integrated in the manuscript. As above, this is positive
evidence of novelty rather than a proof of absolute priority.

## Effective finite-sampling audit

A further search on 8 August 2026 tested the finite-sampling consequence of
the certificate.  The arXiv Atom API returned zero records for both
all:"finite sampling" AND all:Mahler and
all:"dynamical zeta" AND all:"finite samples".  It again returned zero for
all:"rational solutions" AND all:"Mahler equation" and
all:"Mahler coboundary".

Crossref, Semantic Scholar, and zbMATH Open were searched for finite sampling
Mahler function, zeros special values Mahler functions finite sampling,
Pade rational reconstruction Mahler equation, and finite group extension
dynamical zeta inverse finite samples.  The nearest records were:

- Chyzak--Dreyfus--Dumas--Mezzarobba (2018), DOI 10.1090/mcom/3359,
  for algorithms solving linear Mahler equations;
- Arreche--Zhang, *Mahler Discrete Residues and Summability for Rational
  Functions* (ISSAC 2022), DOI 10.1145/3476446.3536186, for additive
  rational summability;
- Pegis (1996), DOI 10.1006/jmaa.1996.0156, for the different equation
  F(z^2)=A F(z)+B+C/F(z);
- Boyle--Schmieding (2017), DOI 10.1017/etds.2015.87, for periodic-data
  invariants of finite-group extensions.

Semantic Scholar resolved all four DOI records; its keyword-search endpoint
was intermittently rate-limited with HTTP 429.  zbMATH Open returned the
linear-solution paper (record 1393.39002), the 2025 first-order-factor paper
(record 1572.11106), and the Mahler-residue paper, but no finite-sampling
inverse theorem.  None of the located works bounds radial collision points by
the degree of a normalized multiplicative Mahler certificate or derives a
finite dynamical-zeta sampling theorem.  This supports, but cannot prove,
the priority of Theorem thm:finite-radial-sampling.

Finally, the requested stronger dependence on only `(graph, group,
Perron-peripheral spectrum)` is mathematically impossible.  The paper gives
two primitive `Z/2` extensions of the same two-vertex graph with the same
Perron-peripheral spectrum `{2}` but spectral cohomology multiplicities `2`
and `1`.  Thus the sharp invariant must retain the full Wedderburn
characteristic data; peripheral data alone cannot be repaired by stronger
mixing or semisimplicity assumptions.

## General-group polynomial sampling audit (10 August 2026)

A fresh search targeted the proposed statement that finitely many algebraic
radial values determine all primitive length--class data for every finite
group, with a sample bound polynomial in the graph size and group order.
The arXiv API query
`("finite sampling" OR "finite determination") AND
("dynamical zeta" OR Mahler)` returned no records.  Broad zbMATH Open
searches for `"finite sampling" Mahler` and
`"dynamical zeta" "finite group" inverse` likewise returned no records.

Crossref and exact-DOI lookups identified two nearest antecedents:

- F. Chyzak, T. Dreyfus, P. Dumas, and M. Mezzarobba, *Computing
  solutions of linear Mahler equations*, Math. Comp. 87 (2018), 2977--3021,
  DOI `10.1090/mcom/3359`, arXiv:`1612.05518`, zbMATH `1393.39002`;
- M. Boyle and S. Schmieding, *Finite group extensions of shifts of finite
  type: K-theory, Parry and Livsic*, ETDS 37 (2017), 2355--2366,
  DOI `10.1017/etds.2015.87`, zbMATH record `6728708`.

The first is the nearest effective Mahler work but concerns linear Mahler
equations.  The second is the nearest dynamical work and studies periodic-data
invariants and non-rigidity for finite-group SFT extensions.  Neither states
an effective inverse theorem for nonlinear multiplicative-coboundary radial
sampling.  Semantic Scholar's keyword endpoint returned HTTP 429 during this
audit, while exact DOI lookups for both records succeeded.  As always, these
database results are evidence about nearest prior work, not proof of absolute
priority.

## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)

The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:

- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
- Kumiko Nishioka, *Mahler Functions and Transcendence* (1996), Theorem 5.1.7,
  is the standard reference for the rational--transcendental dichotomy for
  `k`-Mahler functions defined by a linear functional equation. Bell, Coons and
  Rowland, arXiv:1210.2070v2, Corollary 8, gives an open-access restatement and
  a new proof.
- The equation `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is quadratic in `F` and therefore
  outside that linear class. Keiji Nishioka's 1985 nonlinear class
  `f(z^p) = R(z,f(z))` is the applicable result, with `p = 2` and
  `R(z,Y) = Y^2/H(z)`. This algebraic-to-rational step is prior work and is not
  a contribution of the paper.
- Springer keeps the cited 1985 pages 330--335 behind subscription, and
  Unpaywall reported no open-access copy; this audit does not record a
  first-hand check of the printed text.
- The paper's claimed Mahler contribution is limited to the input-only divisor
  estimate for the multiplicative certificate, its sharp lower-bound family
  and realizable transfer, and the supporting explicit height and fixed-base
  integer bit analysis. Bare existence and decidability are prior, and the
  Pade step is largely standard rational reconstruction after a degree cap is
  known. The tier-carrying claim is the cross-base odd-Adams-invariant
  abelian-two-group dynamical inverse theorem.

In particular, the paper does not claim originality for the general
algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,
for Frobenius-class products or equidistribution, or for the general
periodic-data dictionary. This boundary matches the introduction and
conclusion of the present manuscript.

## General-p multiplicative Mahler priority correction (15 August 2026)

A new search was made before extending the effective theorem from `p=2` to
arbitrary fixed `p >= 2`.  It covered the arXiv API, Crossref, the full texts
of arXiv:1612.05518 and arXiv:2403.11545, the author-hosted full text of the
ISSAC 2022 paper below, zbMATH/Open search results, and exact-title web
searches for combinations of `rational solutions`, `Mahler equation`,
`multiplicative`, `summability`, `Riccati`, and `first-order factors`.
OpenAlex returned a depleted daily API budget and ACM's landing page returned
a browser challenge, so neither was treated as negative evidence.  Crossref
metadata and the author-hosted paper supplied the primary record instead.

The decisive antecedents are:

- F. Chyzak, T. Dreyfus, P. Dumas, and M. Mezzarobba, *Computing
  solutions of linear Mahler equations*, Math. Comp. 87 (2018), 2977--3021,
  DOI `10.1090/mcom/3359`, arXiv:`1612.05518`.  Its abstract and Section 3
  give algorithms for rational solutions of linear Mahler equations.
- C. E. Arreche and Y. Zhang, *Mahler Discrete Residues and Summability for
  Rational Functions*, ISSAC 2022, 525--533, DOI
  `10.1145/3476446.3536186`.  Its abstract and Main Theorem give a complete
  effective obstruction to deciding whether a given rational `f(z)` equals
  `g(z^p)-g(z)` for rational `g`.  Its introduction explicitly notes that
  the 2018 linear-Mahler rational-solution algorithm also decides this
  certificate problem.
- F. Chyzak, T. Dreyfus, P. Dumas, and M. Mezzarobba, *First-order factors
  of linear Mahler operators*, J. Symbolic Comput. 130 (2025), 102424, DOI
  `10.1016/j.jsc.2025.102424`, arXiv:`2403.11545`.  Its Riccati monomials are
  products of successive shifts.  It is adjacent, but it is not needed for
  the reduction below.
- C. Pegis, *Rational Solutions of a Nonlinear Functional Equation Related
  to Mahler's Equation*, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 199 (1996), 489--494, DOI
  `10.1006/jmaa.1996.0156`, treats the different equation
  `F(z^2)=A F(z)+B+C/F(z)` with constant coefficients.

The multiplicative decision problem is not formally separate from the first
two algorithms.  Put `H=P0/P1`, let `sigma f(z)=f(z^p)`, and define
`u=z R'/R`.  Direct logarithmic differentiation proves

```
(sigma-1)u = (z/p) H'/H.                                      (1)
```

Thus Arreche--Zhang directly decides and constructs the possible `u`.  The
2018 homogeneous algorithm also applies: for nonzero right-hand side `f`, any
solution of `(sigma-1)u=f` satisfies
`(sigma-(sigma f)/f)(sigma-1)u=0`, after which one filters the rational
solution space by the original affine equation.

The converse is also effective, so this is a reduction rather than a
one-way necessary condition. Additive solutions are determined only up to a
constant. After replacing `u` by its unique representative with `u(0)=0`, it
comes from a normalized `R in Q(z)` exactly when `u/z` is regular at zero,
has no polynomial part, and has only simple finite poles with integer
residues. Necessity
is the standard partial-fraction form of a rational logarithmic derivative.
For sufficiency, Galois invariance groups poles with the same integer residue
into rational irreducible factors; their normalized product gives
`R'/R=u/z` and `R(0)=1`.  Equation (1) then says that
`R(z^p)/(H(z)R(z)^p)` has zero logarithmic derivative.  Its value at zero is
one, so it is identically one.

Consequently, bare decidability of the multiplicative rational-solution
problem is already subsumed after this non-obvious transformation.  The
nontrivial surviving core is the input-only degree bound of sharp order
`D log D` for the multiplicative certificate itself, together with its lower-
bound family and dynamically realizable transfer. The explicit height and
fixed-`p` integer bit bounds are useful quantitative additions. The affine
Pade calculation is a direct implementation of standard rational
reconstruction once the degree cap is known, and exact rejection is necessary
for correctness rather than a separate novelty claim.

 634: For an integer \(p\ge2\) and \(D\ge1\), define
 635: \begin{equation}\label{eq:logarithmic-mahler-bound-definition}
 636:  m_p(D):=\min\{m\ge1:p^m(p-1)\ge2D\},
 637:  \qquad
 638:  b_p(D):=\left\lceil\frac{2D}{p}m_p(D)\right\rceil.
 639: \end{equation}
 640: Let \(P_0,P_1\in\QQ[z]\) be coprime, with constant term one and
 641: \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1>0\).  If a normalized rational function
 642: \[
 643:  R=\frac AB\in\QQ(z)^\times,
 644:  \qquad (A,B)=1,\qquad A(0)=B(0)=1,
 645: \]
 646: satisfies
 647: \begin{equation}\label{eq:p-mahler-coboundary}
 648:  \frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},
 649: \end{equation}
 650: then
 651: \begin{equation}\label{eq:logarithmic-mahler-degree-bound}
 652:  \deg A+\deg B\le b_p(D).
 653: \end{equation}
 654: If \(P_0/P_1\ne1\), the equation \(R(z)=1\) has at most
 655: \(b_p(D)-1\) distinct non-zero complex solutions.  In particular,
 656: \begin{equation}\label{eq:binary-logarithmic-mahler-degree-bound}
 657:  b_2(D)=D\lceil\log_2(2D)\rceil.
 658: \end{equation}
 659: \end{proposition}
 660: 
 661: \begin{proof}
 662: For \(\alpha\in\overline{\QQ}^{\times}\), let
 663: \[
 664:  e(\alpha)=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha}(P_0/P_1),
 665:  \qquad r(\alpha)=\operatorname{ord}_{z=\alpha}R.
 666: \]
 667: The reduced input has
 668: \(\sum_\alpha\abs{e(\alpha)}=D\), while
 669: \(\sum_\alpha\abs{r(\alpha)}=\deg A+\deg B\).  Taking divisors in
 670: \eqref{eq:p-mahler-coboundary} gives
 671: \begin{equation}\label{eq:p-mahler-divisor-recurrence}
 672:  e(\alpha)=r(\alpha^p)-pr(\alpha).
 673: \end{equation}
 674: Iteration along the forward \(p\)-power orbit yields
 675: \[
 676:  r(\alpha)=p^{-n}r(\alpha^{p^n})
 677:  -\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}p^{-j-1}e(\alpha^{p^j}).
 678: \]
 679: The first term tends to zero because \(r\) has finite support.  This remains
 680: true on a periodic root-of-unity orbit, since the numerator is bounded and
 681: the factor \(p^{-n}\) tends to zero.  Hence
 682: \begin{equation}\label{eq:p-mahler-forward-inversion}
 683:  r(\alpha)=-\sum_{j\ge0}p^{-j-1}e(\alpha^{p^j}).
 684: \end{equation}
 685: 
 686: Put \(S=\operatorname{supp}r\) and
 687: \(T=\sum_\alpha\abs{r(\alpha)}\).  For every \(j\),
 688: the map \(\alpha\mapsto\alpha^{p^j}\) on
 689: \(\overline{\QQ}^{\times}\) is exactly \(p^j\)-to-one.  Splitting
 690: \eqref{eq:p-mahler-forward-inversion} at \(m=m_p(D)\), using
 691: \(\#S\le T\) and \(\max_\alpha\abs{e(\alpha)}\le D\), gives
 692: \begin{align*}
 693:  T
 694:  &\le \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}p^{-j-1}
 695:        \sum_{\alpha\in S}\abs{e(\alpha^{p^j})}
 696:    +\sum_{\alpha\in S}\sum_{j\ge m}
 697:        p^{-j-1}\abs{e(\alpha^{p^j})}\\
 698:  &\le \frac{mD}{p}+\frac{TD}{p^m(p-1)}
 699:  \le \frac{mD}{p}+\frac T2.
 700: \end{align*}
 701: Thus \(T\le2mD/p\); integrality of \(T\) proves
 702: \eqref{eq:logarithmic-mahler-degree-bound}.
 703: 
 704: Normalized injectivity of the coboundary map, proved in
 705: \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate}, shows that \(P_0/P_1\ne1\) implies
 706: \(R\ne1\).  The non-zero polynomial \(A-B\) has degree at most
 707: \(\deg A+\deg B\) and vanishes at zero.  It therefore has at most
 708: \(b_p(D)-1\) distinct non-zero roots.  Formula
 709: \eqref{eq:binary-logarithmic-mahler-degree-bound} follows directly from
 710: \eqref{eq:logarithmic-mahler-bound-definition}.
 711: \end{proof}
 712: 
 713: \begin{corollary}[Sharp order of the multiplicative certificate degree]
 714: \label{rem:logarithmic-mahler-degree-sharpness}
 715: Fix \(p\ge2\).  Let \(Q\in\ZZ[z]\) have degree \(q>0\) and \(Q(0)=1\),
 716: and suppose that
 717: \(Q(z^{p^{J+1}})\) and \(Q(z)\) are coprime.  Then
 718: \[
 719:  R_J(z):=\prod_{j=0}^{J}Q(z^{p^j})^{p^{J-j}}
 720: \]
 721: satisfies
 722: \[
 723:  \frac{R_J(z^p)}{R_J(z)^p}
 724:  =\frac{Q(z^{p^{J+1}})}{Q(z)^{p^{J+1}}},
 725:  \qquad
 726:  \deg R_J=(J+1)p^Jq,\qquad D=2p^{J+1}q.
 727: \]
 728: The coprimality hypothesis holds, for example, for \(Q(z)=1-2z\).  In that
 729: case the displayed numerator and denominator are coprime integer polynomials
 730: with constant term one.  As \(J\to\infty\), their unique normalized rational
 731: solution therefore has degree \(\Omega_p(D\log D)\).  Thus the order
 732: \(D\log D\) cannot be replaced by \(o(D\log D)\) for integer inputs.
 733: \end{corollary}
 734: 
 735: The preceding proposition and sharpness corollary contain the nontrivial
 736: quantitative core: an input-only degree estimate for the multiplicative
 737: certificate itself, with optimal order.  The following strong supporting
 738: theorem retains all useful effective consequences in one place.  Its bare
 739: existence and decidability assertions also follow from the cited additive and
 740: linear Mahler algorithms, while its Pad\'e step is direct rational
 741: reconstruction once the degree cap is available.  The explicit height and
 742: fixed-\(p\) bit bounds are the additional quantitative layer.  For an integral
 743: polynomial \(P\), write
 744: \[
 745:  h(P):=\log\max_j\abs{[z^j]P}.
 746: \]

 succeeded in 292ms:
 250: to the reduced input pair.  A non-coprime determinant ratio may first be
 251: cancelled, but no unchanged-height assertion for the uncancelled pair is
 252: being made here.
 253: \end{proof}

 255: \begin{theorem}[Unconditional interior finite sampling and collision dichotomy]
 256: \label{thm:finite-radial-sampling}
 257: Let \(G=C_2\), and let
 258: \(\tau,\tau':E(\Gamma)\to C_2\) be two labellings on the same marked
 259: directed multigraph with primitive base matrix \(A\), Perron root
 260: \(\lambda>1\), and sign blocks \(B,B'\).  Put \(x=\lambda^{-1}\), and set
 261: \[
 262:  \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
 263:  :=F_\varepsilon^\tau(y)-F_\varepsilon^{\tau'}(y)
 264:  \qquad(0<y<x).
 265: \]
 266: For
 267: \(C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)\), the corresponding pairwise radial
 268: class-profile difference is
 269: \[
 270:  \mathcal D_C(y):=\sum_{n\ge1}
 271:  \bigl(p_{n,C}(\tau)-p_{n,C}(\tau')\bigr)\log(1-y^n);
 272: \]
 273: both series converge absolutely for \(0<y<x\).  Write
 274: \[
 275:  H(z):=\frac{\det(I-zB)}{\det(I-zB')}
 276:       =\frac{P_0(z)}{P_1(z)}
 277: \]
 278: in reduced form with coprime \(P_0,P_1\in\ZZ[z]\) and
 279: \(P_0(0)=P_1(0)=1\), and put \(D=\deg P_0+\deg P_1\).
 280: Equivalently, \(H=\zeta_{\widetilde X_{\tau'}}/
 281: \zeta_{\widetilde X_\tau}\) by \Cref{prop:c2-standard-zeta-ratio}.
 282: 
 283: If \(D=0\), then the two labellings have identical primitive
 284: length--class profiles.  If \(D>0\), define
 285: \[
 286:  N=D\lceil\log_2(2D)\rceil.
 287: \]
 288: \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}
 289:  \#\{y\in\overline{\QQ}\cap(0,x):
 290:           \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}\le N-1.
 291: \end{equation}
 292: If the set in
 293: \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is non-empty, then the
 294: finite Pad\'e procedure of
 295: \Cref{thm:effective-rational-mahler-coboundary} constructs the unique reduced
 296: \[
 297:  R=\frac{A_0}{B_0}\in\QQ(z)^\times,
 298:  \qquad A_0(0)=B_0(0)=1,
 299:  \qquad \deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N,
 300: \]
 301: for which \(H(z)=R(z^2)/R(z)^2\).  The complete real collision set is then
 302: \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}
 303:  \{y\in(0,x):\Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\}
 304:  =\{y\in(0,x):A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0\}.
 305: \end{equation}
 306: In this case the complete real collision set has at most \(N-1\) elements.
 307: Consequently, if \(v\) is the size of the base matrix and
 308: \[
 309:  N_*=2v\lceil\log_2(4v)\rceil,
 310: \]
 311: then equality at any \(N_*\) distinct radii
 312: \(y_1,\ldots,y_{N_*}\in(0,x)\), meaning
 313: \(\Delta_\varepsilon(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\), at least one of which is
 314: algebraic, forces
 315: \[
 316:  p_{n,C}(\tau)=p_{n,C}(\tau')
 317:  \qquad(n\ge1,\ C\in\operatorname{Conj}(C_2)).
 318: \]
 319: Equivalently, simultaneous vanishing of
 320: \(\mathcal D_{\{e\}}\) and \(\mathcal D_{\{s\}}\) at \(N_*\) such radii
 321: recovers the entire primitive length--class profile.
 322: If \(\rad(B),\rad(B')<\lambda\), the assertions about
 323: \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) and the equivalent centered class-profile differences
 324: remain valid on \((0,x]\).  No raw class profile is assigned a finite value at
 325: \(x\).
 326: \end{theorem}
 327: 
 328: \begin{proof}
 329: Every primitive length-\(n\) orbit contributes \(n\) period-\(n\) points, so
 330: \(np_{n,C}\le\Tr(A^n)=O(\lambda^n)\).  This proves the asserted absolute
 331: convergence at every \(y<x\).
 332: 
 333: The base is fixed, so its trivial determinant coordinate is the same for
 334: \(\tau\) and \(\tau'\).  The \(C_2\) Adams--M\"obius reduction used in
 335: \eqref{eq:c2-collision-dyadic-reduction}, now with arbitrary sign blocks,
 336: therefore gives
 337: \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}
 338:  \Delta_\varepsilon(y)
 339:  =-\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H(y^{2^j})
 340:  =-\log\Pi_y(H)
 341:  \qquad(0<y<x).
 342: \end{equation}
 343: The Perron-weighted domination estimate gives
 344: \(\rad(B),\rad(B')\le\lambda\).  Hence both determinant polynomials are
 345: zero-free on \(\abs z<x\), are positive on \([0,y]\) for each \(y<x\), and
 346: the series in \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity} converges there.
 347: Thus
 348: \[
 349:  \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Pi_y(H)=1.
 350: \]
 351: 
 352: If \(D=0\), then \(H=1\).  The trivial and sign determinant coordinates are
 353: both equal, so \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary} gives equality of all
 354: primitive length--class data.  The same conclusion holds whenever \(H=1\).
 355: 
 356: Suppose now that \(H\ne1\).  If there is no algebraic collision radius,
 357: \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound} is immediate.  Otherwise
 358: choose one such radius \(y_0\).  The algebraic-radius form of
 359: \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} gives a unique normalized
 360: \(R\in\QQ(z)^\times\) with
 361: \[
 362:  H(z)=\frac{R(z^2)}{R(z)^2},
 363:  \qquad R(y_0)=1.
 364: \]
 365: The effective criterion constructs its reduced numerator and denominator
 366: \(A_0,B_0\) and gives \(\deg A_0+\deg B_0\le N\).
 367: 
 368: For every real \(0<y<x\),
 369: \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate} applies on \([0,y]\) and gives
 370: \(\Pi_y(H)=R(y)^{-2}\) with \(R(y)>0\).  Hence
 371: \[
 372:  \Delta_\varepsilon(y)=0
 373:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 374:  R(y)=1
 375:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 376:  A_0(y)-B_0(y)=0,
 377: \]
 378: which proves \eqref{eq:finite-radial-complete-collision-set}.  Since \(H\ne1\),
 379: the polynomial \(A_0-B_0\) is non-zero.  Its degree is at most \(N\), while
 380: \(A_0(0)-B_0(0)=0\).  It therefore has at most \(N-1\) distinct non-zero
 381: roots, proving \eqref{eq:finite-radial-algebraic-collision-bound}.
 382: 
 383: Each determinant has degree at most \(v\), so reduction gives \(D\le2v\).
 384: The displayed function defining \(N\) is increasing in the positive integer
 385: \(D\); hence \(N\le N_*\).  If \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) vanished at \(N_*\)
 386: distinct radii, one of which is algebraic, the complete real collision-set
 387: bound \(N-1<N_*\) would be contradicted when \(H\ne1\).  Thus \(H=1\), and
 388: the periodic data dictionary gives the
 389: asserted recovery.  Finally, for \(C_2=\{e,s\}\)
 390: the fixed base gives equality of the scalar coordinate, while
 391: \(\mathbf1_{\{e\}}=(\mathbf1+\varepsilon)/2\) and
 392: \(\mathbf1_{\{s\}}=(\mathbf1-\varepsilon)/2\).  Therefore equality of
 393: \(\Delta_\varepsilon(y)\) is equivalent to
 394: \(\mathcal D_{\{e\}}(y)=\mathcal D_{\{s\}}(y)=0\), proving the last
 395: assertion.
 396: 
 397: If both sign blocks have strict spectral radius below \(\lambda\), their
 398: determinants are zero-free on a disk strictly larger than \(\abs z\le x\).
 399: The identity \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}, the lifting theorem,
 400: and the rational telescoping formula then hold also at \(x\).  Since the base
 401: is common, the class-profile differences equal the differences of the centered
 402: profiles.  This gives precisely the asserted centered endpoint extension.
 403: \end{proof}
 404: 
 405: \begin{theorem}[Rank-independent radial locations for elementary two-groups]
 406: \label{thm:elementary-two-group-finite-sampling}
 407: Let \(E=(C_2)^r\), with \(r\ge0\).  Let
 408: \(\tau:E(\Gamma)\to E\) and \(\tau':E(\Gamma')\to E\) be one-step
 409: cocycles over primitive non-negative integral base matrices \(A,A'\), whose
 410: sizes are at most \(V\) and whose Perron roots \(\lambda,\lambda'>1\) need
 411: not agree.  Put
 412: \[
 413:  x=\min\{\lambda^{-1},(\lambda')^{-1}\},
 414:  \qquad M(V)=2V\lceil\log_2(4V)\rceil.
 415: \]
 416: For \(g\in E\), define
 417: \[
 418:  \mathcal E_g^\tau(y)=\sum_{n\ge1}p_{n,g}(\tau)\log(1-y^n),
 419:  \qquad 0<y<x,
 420: \]
 421: and define \(\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}\) analogously.  Suppose that
 422: \[
 423:  \mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)=\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
 424:  \qquad(g\in E,\ 1\le i\le M(V))
 425: \]
 426: at \(M(V)\) distinct radii in \((0,x)\), at least one of which is
 427: algebraic.  Then
 428: \[
 429:  p_{n,g}(\tau)=p_{n,g}(\tau')
 430:  \qquad(n\ge1,\ g\in E).
 431: \]
 432: One radial observation here means the full vector
 433: \((\mathcal E_g(y_i))_{g\in E}\).  Thus the theorem uses \(M(V)\)
 434: radial locations independently of \(r\), while the total number of scalar
 435: equalities assumed is \(|E|M(V)=2^rM(V)\).  Neither a common base
 436: presentation nor a strict spectral gap for the non-trivial character blocks
 437: is required.
 438: \end{theorem}
 439: 
 440: \begin{proof}
 441: Absolute convergence follows for each system from the periodic-point estimate
 442: used in \Cref{thm:finite-radial-sampling}.  Summing the assumed identities over
 443: \(g\in E\) gives, at every sampled radius,
 444: \[
 445:  \log\det(I-y_iA)=\sum_{g\in E}\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)
 446:  =\sum_{g\in E}\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)
 447:  =\log\det(I-y_iA').
 448: \]
 449: Both determinants are positive on \((0,x)\).  Their difference has degree at
 450: most \(V\), vanishes at the \(M(V)\ge V\) distinct non-zero sample points,
 451: and also vanishes at zero.  Hence
 452: \begin{equation}\label{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}
 453:  \det(I-zA)=\det(I-zA').
 454: \end{equation}
 455: 
 456: Every \(\chi\in\widehat E\) takes values in \(\{\pm1\}\).  Let
 457: \(B_{\chi,\tau}\) and \(B_{\chi,\tau'}\) be the corresponding character
 458: blocks and put
 459: \[
 460:  H_\chi(z)=\frac{\det(I-zB_{\chi,\tau})}
 461:                   {\det(I-zB_{\chi,\tau'})}.
 462: \]
 463: Since \(\chi(g)\equiv1\pmod2\), entrywise reduction gives
 464: \[
 465:  B_{\chi,\tau}\equiv A\pmod2,
 466:  \qquad B_{\chi,\tau'}\equiv A'\pmod2.
 467: \]
 468: Together with \eqref{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}, this
 469: shows that the two character determinants are congruent modulo two and hence
 470: supports the integral refinement in
 471: \Cref{lem:critical-mahler-integrality}; the two blocks need not have the same
 472: size.  This congruence is not an input to the parity-free lifting theorem
 473: \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} used below.
 474: 
 475: Fourier transformation of the sampled class-profile identities gives
 476: \[
 477:  \Delta_\chi(y_i):=
 478:  \sum_{g\in E}\chi(g)
 479:  \bigl(\mathcal E_g^\tau(y_i)-\mathcal E_g^{\tau'}(y_i)\bigr)=0.
 480: \]
 481: For the trivial character this is already
 482: \eqref{eq:elementary-two-group-base-determinant-equality}.  For non-trivial
 483: \(\chi\), one has \(\chi^m=\chi\) for odd \(m\) and
 484: \(\chi^m=\mathbf1\) for even \(m\).  The Adams--M\"obius calculation in
 485: \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}, with the now common trivial
 486: determinant coordinate, therefore gives
 487: \[
 488:  \Delta_\chi(y)=\sum_{j\ge0}2^{-j}\log H_\chi(y^{2^j}).
 489: \]
 490: 
 491: Choose an algebraic sampled radius \(y_0\).  If \(H_\chi\ne1\),
 492: \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting} supplies the unique normalized
 493: \(R_\chi\in\QQ(z)^\times\) such that
 494: \[
 495:  H_\chi(z)=\frac{R_\chi(z^2)}{R_\chi(z)^2},
 496:  \qquad R_\chi(y_0)=1.
 497: \]
 498: Write the reduced ratio \(H_\chi=P_{0,\chi}/P_{1,\chi}\) and put
 499: \(D_\chi=\deg P_{0,\chi}+\deg P_{1,\chi}\).  Both character determinants
 500: have degree at most \(V\), so \(D_\chi\le2V\).  By
 501: \Cref{prop:logarithmic-mahler-divisor-bound} and the positive telescoping
 502: identity in \Cref{prop:rational-mahler-certificate}, all real zeros of
 503: \(\Delta_\chi\) lie among the non-zero roots of \(R_\chi-1\), of which there
 504: are at most
 505: \[
 506:  D_\chi\lceil\log_2(2D_\chi)\rceil-1
 507:  \le M(V)-1.
 508: \]
 509: The \(M(V)\) sampled zeros are therefore impossible.  Thus \(H_\chi=1\)
 510: for every character \(\chi\).  The cross-base periodic-data dictionary in
 511: \Cref{prop:comparison-dictionary}, followed by character Fourier inversion,
 512: now gives equality of every primitive length--element count.
 513: \end{proof}

 515: \begin{remark}[Located obstruction for general finite groups]
 516: \label{rem:general-group-finite-sampling-interface}
 517: For a same-base pair and \(\pi\in\Irr(G)\), put
 518: \(H_\pi=P_{\pi,\tau}/P_{\pi,\tau'}\); then \(H_{\mathbf1}=1\).
 519: Rearranging \eqref{eq:fixed-determinant-open-disc} by \(k=rm\) gives
 520: \begin{equation}\label{eq:general-group-adams-mobius-obstruction}
 521:  \begin{aligned}
 522:  F_{\chi_\rho}^\tau(z)-F_{\chi_\rho}^{\tau'}(z)
 523:    &=-\sum_{k\ge1}\frac1k\sum_{\pi\in\Irr(G)}
 524:        b_{\rho,\pi}(k)\Log_0H_\pi(z^k),\\
 525:  b_{\rho,\pi}(k)
 526:    &=\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)a_{\rho,\pi}^{(m)}.
 527:  \end{aligned}
 528: \end{equation}
 529: For \(C_2\), projection away from the common trivial channel makes these
 530: coefficients vanish unless \(k\) is a power of two.  That lacunarity is exactly
 531: what produces the scalar Mahler product in
 532: \eqref{eq:finite-radial-boundary-identity}.
 533: 
 534: It already fails for \(C_3=\langle g\rangle\).  If \(\chi(g)=\omega\), record
 535: the Adams states in the ordered basis
 536: \((\mathbf1,\chi,\chi^2)\).  Their M\"obius transform is
 537: \[
 538:  \mathbf b(k)=\sum_{m\mid k}\mu(m)e_{m\bmod3}.
 539: \]
 540: For a prime \(p\), this is zero when \(p\equiv1\pmod3\), equals
 541: \(e_1-e_2\) when \(p\equiv2\pmod3\), and equals \(e_1-e_0\) when
 542: \(p=3\).  There are infinitely many primes congruent to two modulo three:
 543: if \(p_1,\ldots,p_r\) were all of them, any prime divisor congruent to two
 544: modulo three of \(3p_1\cdots p_r-1\) would be new.  Thus
 545: \eqref{eq:general-group-adams-mobius-obstruction} couples the two non-trivial
 546: determinant ratios at infinitely many arithmetically distributed powers and
 547: does not satisfy the scalar finite-degree Mahler equation used in
 548: \Cref{thm:determinant-boundary-lifting}.
 549: 
 550: Accordingly the proof of a polynomial radial sampling bound for every finite
 551: group stops here.  The missing input is a special-value theorem forcing
 552: rationality from one algebraic common collision for this coupled cyclotomic
 553: Euler system, together with an effective degree or zero bound for the resulting
 554: certificate.  Neither the scalar lifting theorem nor the Pad\'e bound proved
 555: above supplies that input.  The finite computation in
 556: \Cref{sec:exactness} only checks the displayed \(C_3\) coefficients in a
 557: finite range.
 558: \end{remark}
 559: 
 560: This mechanism is strictly weaker than full \(G\)-cospectrality, equivalently
 561: represented cospectrality in every irreducible representation:
 562: \eqref{eq:c2-collision-first-determinant} and
 563: \eqref{eq:c2-collision-second-determinant} are different.  Represented
 564: cospectrality in every irreducible representation instead requires equality
 565: of the full twisted spectra and therefore preserves the complete periodic profile
 566: \cite{BoyleSchmieding2017FiniteGroupExtensions,
 567: CavaleriDonno2022Cospectrality}.
 568: 
 569: Although one centered Perron-point vector loses information, an analytic radial profile
 570: restores it.  The following is a sufficient recovery criterion; no optimality

 450: \(R=F^{-1}\) in the displayed functional equation gives
 451: \[
 452:  H(z)=\frac{R(z^p)}{R(z)^p},\qquad R(0)=1.
 453: \]
 454: For uniqueness, if \(U(0)=1\) and \(U(z^p)=U(z)^p\), a least non-constant
 455: term \(az^n\) would occur in degree \(pn\) on the left and degree \(n\) on
 456: the right.  Hence \(U=1\).  The rationality implication used here is the cited
 457: result of Keiji Nishioka; the only descent specific to the present
 458: normalization is from the rational Taylor germ to \(\QQ(z)\).
 459: \end{proof}
